target_customer: Engineers at hardware, aerospace and manufacturing companies who run CFD and other physics simulations
problem: Physics simulations and physical prototypes are slow and expensive and need specialist setup. Godela offers AI models that answer simulation questions in natural language.
business_model: B2B software platform, pricing not found

education: Research at Harvard (physics-driven optimization) and Stanford (generative models for fluid mechanics); degrees not stated

technical_complexity.rationale: Physics-informed ML models that match solver accuracy across geometries need research-level modeling and training data, though surrogate modeling was an established field by 2025.

defensibility.rationale: Model quality could be a lead but well-funded rivals and open model families (such as NVIDIA's Apollo, per a 2025-2026 NVIDIA post) lower the barrier. Switching costs depend on integration with engineers' workflows, which was not shown.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not determined. Search results indicate large simulation vendors and NVIDIA moving into AI physics, but dates vs founding are unclear.

market_need_then: Engineering simulation is a large, established spend, and search coverage shows heavy funding for AI physics startups such as PhysicsX and Luminary Cloud in 2025, indicating demand for faster simulation. The founders say the product complements existing simulation.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, ask and get simulation quality results

brand_strength.rationale: Only launch coverage (American Bazaar on 2025-06-03, YC launch page) and investor posts mention it. No evidence of brand-driven traction.

outcome_analysis: Godela is an active Spring 2025 company with founders who built surrogate models at Intel and researched physics ML at Stanford and Harvard, and it announced a launch in June 2025 plus backing from Network VC and CLAI Ventures. Amounts are undisclosed, and no failure or exit news exists, so the outcome is still open.
